problem: Prior scene-graph methods for target-driven / object-goal visual navigation use co-occurrence graphs (e.g., from Visual Genome) with equally weighted, fixed edges, lacking directional spatial relations and node-edge interaction, so they generalize poorly to unseen scenes and add useless state information.
motivation: Directional priors (e.g. remote is under the TV, mouse is right of laptop) can tell an agent which way to turn when the target is invisible. Fixed offline co-occurrence graphs mismatch simulated/real layouts, so a graph that is built per scene and reasoned over with relation-aware attention should guide RL policies better.
key_idea: Build a Heterogeneous Zone Graph with 7 directional relation types from AI2THOR exploration, and encode it with a Relation-wise Transformer (node-to-node self-attention encoder, edge-to-node cross-attention decoder) whose output feeds the critic of an A3C agent.
insight: Table 5 ablations show HZG and RTNet both matter: without HZG (RTNet) SR 34.5 / SPL 7.8 versus 71.6 / 42.5 for the full model, and performance rises as the HZG proportion grows (25% to 75%: SR 56.2 to 60.5). Removing zero-shot/meta adaptation drops SR to 21.0. DETR features beat Faster-RCNN (SR 71.6 vs 67.2). Caveat: the HZG is built from simulator ground-truth spatial knowledge, so the gains partly reflect privileged priors.
method: Heterogeneous Zone Graph (HZG): the agent explores each room randomly, records DETR object bag-of-words plus pose (x,z,yaw,pitch) and ROI features, and k-means clusters them into K zones. Directional relations (7 types) are counted by center-point word frequency (appearing at least 3 times) and stored as a 92x92 adjacency with channels for the 4 room types.

Relationship representation: for each object pair, a vector concatenates projected visual features, a union-box ROIAlign feature added to a bbox-mapped feature, and GloVe semantic embeddings of the two categories.

Encoder N2N attention: nodes (visual feature, semantic embedding, box) are linearly projected, given sinusoidal position, and passed through a transformer encoder. A classifier predicts object class, which supervises node features.

Decoder E2N attention: edge queries are built from union box, visual feature and two GloVe label embeddings. A new edge positional encoding derived from the positions of the two nodes is added, and cross-attention over all nodes gives context-rich edge features.

A3C policy with multimodal fusion: ResNet18 observation, target GloVe, previous action, LSTM memory and RTNet graph embedding form the state. The RTNet graph output expands the critic head; the actor gives 6 actions.
Zero-shot/meta-learning adaptation (SAVN-style): a learned loss is adapted at test time to update the knowledge graph and correct wrong priors in unseen scenes.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 + DETR detector + GloVe + RTNet (transformer) + A3C actor-critic with LSTM, trained from scratch (ResNet18 pretrained)
setting.training_data: AI2THOR: 120 rooms (30 per type; 20 train / 5 val / 5 test per type), SAVN protocol, up to 200M frames; AVD 8 training houses; Habitat Gibson 72 training scenes
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (plus AI2THOR depth to derive 3D boxes for HZG construction)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (main); Active Vision Dataset; Habitat with Gibson scenes
setting.privileged: HZG built from ground-truth object relations/positions in AI2THOR exploration (paper says spatial info is 'extracted from GT scene')

numbers_note: Benchmarks are non-standard (AI2THOR SAVN-style, AVD, Gibson via VGM), none in the canonical list. Table 8 SR values were printed as fractions. Table 3 and Table 4 'Ours' numbers are identical to each other and to the Table 5 full model.
results: On AI2THOR, the method reaches SR 71.6 / SPL 42.5 (Table 4), beating HOZ (70.6 / 40.0) and TPN (69.3 / 39.4) and far exceeding SAVN (40.9 / 16.2). On AVD it gets average SR 31.5 / SPL 16.2 versus Bayes 22.1 / 6.7, and on Gibson-Habitat overall SR 0.88 versus VGM 0.85.
limitations: HZG relies on ground-truth spatial knowledge from simulator exploration of each room type, which limits real-world applicability; sim2real is untested on a robot.
Long training (up to 100–200M frames), and failures with tiny targets, corners, low texture and strong light.
Baseline tables have inconsistencies (e.g. GTN and GVE rows identical), and the paper is loosely written, so comparisons are less reliable.
